title: HTML Max Charachters in Blogs
text: We have migrated to Shopify and are super happy after going live last week. The one area where I have a challenge, however, is that we have a few dozen pages that I need to dump some frankenstein HTML into to keep the styling as it was in our previous site. However, I found that for many of the pages, I couldn’t save the draft and publish it to the site. It turned out it wasn’t able to handle all that HTML. title: Shopify's /products.json returns alt: null for images that do have alt text
text: I was building an alt text audit and hit something worth flagging, because it quietly breaks any audit built on the public product feed. Setup: one product, one image, alt text filled in via admin. Two ways to read the same image: /products/{handle} renders: an img tag with alt=“White wireless earbuds product photo” /products.json returns: “images”: [{ “id”: 123, “alt”: null }] Same image. The rendered page has the description. The JSON says null. Why this matters /products.json is the obvious data source for any bulk audit — one request, structured output, no scraping. But if you build the coverage number on it, you will report that image as missing alt text. The merchant opens their product page, sees alt text right there, and concludes the tool is broken. One false positive and every other number on the page becomes suspect. What I think is happening The feed reports alt from the product media object. Themes often render alt from somewhere else — theme settings, a metafield, or a Liquid fallback that composes a string from the title. So the stored value and the rendered value can disagree, and the feed only knows the stored one. What I’d suggest if you are auditing Use /products.json for counts. How many products, how many images. It is accurate for that. Read alt from the rendered product page if you need the real coverage number. Or read the media object through the Admin API, which is authoritative for what is stored rather than what is displayed. Has anyone else run into this? I am curious whether it is specific to certain themes or a general behaviour of the feed. If you have a store where the two agree, that would be useful to know too. 3 posts - 3 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Bug in Shopify public product feed returning null for alt text.

title: Major Accounting Inconsistencies
text: We seek help understanding the root cause of unexpected General Ledger (GL) and Payment Ledger Entry (PLE) behaviour. We have reconciled and corrected most identified cases in one company, but have not proven why they arose or whether the common factor is standard ERPNext, custom code, deployment history, or a combination. Column 1 Column 2 Column 3 Column 4 Environment ERPNext v16 / Frappe v16, MariaDB, Docker on OVH; multiple companies/sites; several custom apps. Custom apps do not post any transaction. They are majorly reporting tools Main symptoms Repeated GL postings for one submitted invoice; active GL/PLE against Draft vouchers; cancelled vouchers retaining active ledger effects; contradictory document status. Company A scope 293 classified exceptions: 268 duplicate-GL cases plus 25 other cases (reconciled Production audit). Correction evidence 268 duplicates corrected through native Repost Accounting Ledger; 19 additional cases corrected; two cancelled-invoice PLE cases corrected. Last reported state 289/293 corrected in Production; three further methods passed UAT and were authorised for Production, but their Production result is not in the available evidence; one status-conflict invoice remains blocked. 1 What users experienced Invoices were shown as Submitted or Draft, but the ledgers did not always reflect that state. Some submitted invoices had two to four sets of accounting entries even though the PLE or customer outstanding reflected only one invoice. Other Draft transactions had posted GL entries. Some cancelled documents retained open PLE or active GL rows. As a result, GL, receivables/payables and source documents could disagree. 7 posts - 4 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Accounting inconsistencies between General Ledger and Payment Ledger entries.
